OUT = Path('outputs')
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
GENERATOR = r'''from pathlib import Path
import csv
import json
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import TwoSlopeNorm
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

def locate(name):
    candidates = [ROOT / "assets" / "assets" / name, ROOT / "assets" / name, Path("assets/assets") / name, Path("assets") / name]
    for path in candidates:
        if path.exists():
            return path
    raise FileNotFoundError(name)

csv_path = locate("table4_utkface.csv")
manifest_path = locate("table4_manifest.json")

with csv_path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as handle:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(handle))
with manifest_path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    provenance = json.load(handle)

methods = provenance["methods"]
columns = provenance["columns"]
assert len(methods) == 10 and len(columns) == 14
assert len(provenance["cells"]) == 140
by_method = {row["Method"]: row for row in rows}
strings = [[by_method[m][c] for c in columns] for m in methods]
values = [[float(v) for v in row] for row in strings]
for m, row in zip(methods, strings):
    for c, source_string in zip(columns, row):
        cell = provenance["cells"][f"{m}|{c}"]
        assert cell["value"] == source_string
        assert cell["locator"].startswith("S4.T4.6.1.")

plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "axes.titleweight": "bold"})
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(20, 10.8), constrained_layout=False)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.12, right=0.91, top=0.76, bottom=0.18)
norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-4.5, vcenter=0.0, vmax=1.0)
im = ax.imshow(values, cmap="RdYlBu", norm=norm, aspect="auto", interpolation="nearest")

ax.set_xticks(range(len(columns)), labels=columns, rotation=42, ha="right", rotation_mode="anchor", fontsize=10.5)
ax.xaxis.tick_top()
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0, pad=8)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(methods)), labels=methods, fontsize=12)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0, pad=8)
ax.set_xticks([x - 0.5 for x in range(1, len(columns))], minor=True)
ax.set_yticks([y - 0.5 for y in range(1, len(methods))], minor=True)
ax.grid(which="minor", color="white", linewidth=1.25, alpha=0.9)
ax.tick_params(which="minor", bottom=False, left=False)
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)

for i, row in enumerate(strings):
    for j, source_string in enumerate(row):
        rgba = im.cmap(im.norm(float(source_string)))
        luminance = 0.2126 * rgba[0] + 0.7152 * rgba[1] + 0.0722 * rgba[2]
        color = "#111827" if luminance > 0.57 else "white"
        ax.text(j, i, source_string, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9.2, color=color, fontweight="semibold")

mean_idx = columns.index("Mean")
ax.axvline(mean_idx - 0.5, color="#111827", linewidth=3.0)
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((mean_idx - 0.5, -0.5), 1, len(methods), fill=False, edgecolor="#111827", linewidth=2.1))
oracle_idx = methods.index("Oracle")
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((-0.5, oracle_idx - 0.5), len(columns), 1, fill=False, edgecolor="#7c3f00", linewidth=3.0))
ax.text(len(columns) - 0.45, oracle_idx, " label-using upper bound", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=10.5, color="#7c3f00", fontweight="bold", clip_on=False)

fig.suptitle("UTKFace robustness at corruption severity 5", x=0.12, y=0.965, ha="left", fontsize=23, fontweight="bold", color="#111827")
fig.text(0.12, 0.91, "Test R² (unitless; higher is better) • exact source-reported strings shown in every cell", ha="left", fontsize=13, color="#374151")
fig.text(0.12, 0.865, "13 ImageNet-C corruption types", ha="left", fontsize=11.5, color="#4b5563")
fig.text(0.88, 0.865, "REPORTED SUMMARY", ha="center", fontsize=10.5, color="#111827", fontweight="bold")
fig.text(0.12, 0.075, "Color is centered at R² = 0 so negative values remain visually explicit. Mean is the reported across-corruption summary, not an independent run.", ha="left", fontsize=11, color="#374151")
fig.text(0.12, 0.043, "No run-level observations, dispersion, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests are available.", ha="left", fontsize=10.5, color="#6b7280")

cbar_ax = fig.add_axes([0.925, 0.25, 0.015, 0.40])
cbar = fig.colorbar(im, cax=cbar_ax, ticks=[-4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 0.5, 1.0])
cbar.set_label("Test R²", fontsize=11)
cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=9)

figure_path = OUT / "utkface_table4_heatmap.png"
fig.savefig(figure_path, dpi=220, facecolor="white", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

caption = """# Caption

**Figure 1. UTKFace age prediction under image corruption.** The matrix shows source-reported test R² (unitless; higher is better) for all 10 methods across 13 ImageNet-C corruption types at severity 5 and the reported Mean; source training used original images [E1: Section 4.3.2, Table 4 caption S4.T4.5; Appendix B A2.p1/A2.E12; direction S4.T2.5] [E4: Section 4.1, S4.SS1.p3]. Exact three-decimal source strings are printed in cells, and the zero-centered diverging scale visibly retains negative values. These entries are reported table summaries: Appendix C states that each TTA was run with three random seeds and mean scores reported, but individual runs and dispersion are absent, and that protocol is not established by this evidence for Source, TTT, DANN, or Oracle; the Mean column is an across-corruption summary, not an independent run [E2: Table 4 rows S4.T4.6.1.2–11; Appendix C A3.SS3.p1; comparator categories S4.SS2.p3]. Oracle is outlined separately because it fine-tunes with test labels and is an upper-bound comparator [E3: S4.SS2.p3]. For Pixelate, FR = 0.946, RSD = 0.941, and SSA = 0.943 [E3: S4.T4.6.1.7.8, S4.T4.6.1.9.8, S4.T4.6.1.10.8].
"""
interpretation = """# Interpretation

The reported Mean is highest for Oracle (0.789), the label-using upper-bound comparator, and is 0.731 for SSA. Among the displayed non-Oracle rows, SSA has the highest reported Mean. Its largest descriptive advantages over FR occur for the three noise corruptions: Gaussian noise (0.580 versus 0.509), impulse noise (0.592 versus 0.522), and shot noise (0.560 versus 0.458). The pattern is not universal. On Pixelate, FR is highest among those two methods at 0.946, compared with SSA at 0.943; RSD is 0.941. FR and SSA tie at 0.839 on motion blur and at 0.899 on elastic transform, while SSA and RSD tie at 0.851 on zoom blur.

Negative R² values remain explicit in both color and text. They are concentrated for Source, DANN, Prototype, and VM, although their profiles differ by corruption. In particular, DANN reaches -4.341 on Gaussian noise, while Source reaches -3.906 on Contrast. These comparisons describe rounded, source-reported aggregates only. The available evidence supplies neither independent-run observations nor dispersion, so the displayed differences do not support uncertainty intervals, significance claims, causal conclusions, or reconstruction of run-level variation. The three-seed statement applies explicitly to TTA reporting and should not be generalized to every comparator. [E1–E4; locators detailed in the caption and numeric manifest.]
"""
words = interpretation.replace("# Interpretation", "").split()
assert 150 <= len(words) <= 220, len(words)
(OUT / "caption.md").write_text(caption, encoding="utf-8")
(OUT / "interpretation.md").write_text(interpretation, encoding="utf-8")

provenance["visual_encoding"] = {
    "artifact": "utkface_table4_heatmap.png",
    "marks": "one annotated matrix cell per method-column pair",
    "text": "exact source string",
    "color": "continuous diverging encoding of parsed numeric value, centered at zero",
    "mean_separation": "heavy border denotes the reported across-corruption summary",
    "oracle_separation": "outlined row denotes the test-label-using upper-bound comparator",
    "uncertainty": "none encoded because run-level values and dispersion were not supplied"
}
provenance["validation"] = {
    "method_count": len(methods),
    "corruption_count": len(columns) - 1,
    "displayed_cell_count": len(methods) * len(columns),
    "source_string_matches_csv": True,
    "all_cell_locators_present": True
}
with (OUT / "numeric_provenance.json").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    json.dump(provenance, handle, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    handle.write("\n")

print(json.dumps({"figure": str(figure_path), "methods": len(methods), "columns": len(columns), "cells": len(methods) * len(columns), "interpretation_words": len(words)}))
'''
script_path = OUT / 'generate_figure.py'
script_path.write_text(GENERATOR, encoding='utf-8')
namespace = {'__name__': '__main__', '__file__': str(script_path.resolve())}
exec(compile(GENERATOR, str(script_path), 'exec'), namespace)
